mercy_translation.text:
We have already stated, as far as possible and as far as we were able to understand it, part of the reason for his bodily manifestation: it belonged to no one else to change the corruptible into incorruption except the Savior himself, who in the beginning made all things from nothing; it belonged to no one else to recreate in human beings what was according to the image except the Image of the Father; it belonged to no one else to make the mortal immortal except our Lord Jesus Christ, who is Life itself; and it belonged to no one else to teach concerning the Father and overthrow the worship of idols except the Word who orders all things and is the Father's only-begotten and true Son.

But because what was owed by all also had to be paid—for, as I said before, it was owed that all should die, and this was chiefly why he came—after giving demonstrations of his divinity through his works, he then offered the sacrifice on behalf of all, handing over his own temple to death in place of all. He did this so as to make all free and no longer liable to the ancient transgression, and also to show himself stronger than death by displaying his own incorruptible body as the firstfruits of the resurrection of all.

Do not be surprised if we say the same things repeatedly about the same matters. Since we are speaking about the gracious purpose of God, we explain the same subject in several ways lest we seem to leave anything out and incur blame for speaking inadequately. It is better to endure the charge of repetition than to omit something that ought to be written.

The body, then, shared the same nature common to all, for it was a human body. Although by a new wonder it was constituted from the Virgin alone, nevertheless, being mortal, it died in accordance with bodies like it. Yet because of the coming of the Word into it, it no longer underwent corruption according to its own nature; because the Word of God dwelt in it, it was kept outside corruption.

Thus both things happened wonderfully in the same reality: the death of all was fulfilled in the Lord's body, and death and corruption were abolished because of the Word who was present in it. For death was necessary, and a death on behalf of all had to take place so that what was owed by all might be accomplished.

Therefore, as I said before, since the Word himself could not die—for he was immortal—he took to himself a body capable of dying, so that he might offer it as his own in place of all; and, as himself suffering on behalf of all because of his union with it, he might “destroy the one who had the power of death, that is, the devil, and free those who through fear of death were subject to slavery throughout their lives.”

translator_notes: Translated directly from the Greek source.
Athanasius brings together image-restoration, immortality, revelation of the Father, and sacrificial death as dimensions of the Incarnation.
The body is both truly mortal and preserved from corruption because of the indwelling Word.
